sectors.name: Arms & Munitions
sectors.blurb: Nobody has ever gone broke selling ordnance to three sides at once.

sectors.name: Hauling & Portage
sectors.blurb: Freight. Boring until the lanes close, and then it is the only story.

sectors.name: Fuel & Reaction Mass
sectors.blurb: Everything burns something. Vorrn-7 and Cindermoor between them price the Expanse.

sectors.name: Mining & Materials
sectors.blurb: Ferrocrystal, verdite, ore. Dug out of places people die in.

sectors.name: Salvage & Parts
sectors.blurb: A rift bloom is a tragedy and a restock. Ossuary does not pretend otherwise.

sectors.name: Relic Ventures
sectors.blurb: Ancient tech, pilgrim money, and a great deal of confident nonsense.

sectors.name: Medical & Bio
sectors.blurb: Wounded people are a growth market and everyone knows it.

sectors.name: Synthesis & Supply
sectors.blurb: Air, water, protein. The least glamorous money in the Expanse and the most reliable.

sectors.name: Vice & Luxury
sectors.blurb: Drink, tables, and the sort of cargo that does not like a customs officer.

sectors.name: Security & Bonding
sectors.blurb: Escorts, bounties and underwriting. Thrives on danger, dies on order.

companies.name: Vorrn Skimworks
companies.blurb: Skims the gas giant for reaction mass and sells it to anyone who lands. As close to a utility as this sector has.

companies.name: Halberd's Rest Portage
companies.blurb: Runs the docks inside the gutted Directorate dreadnought. Everything that crosses the Expanse is weighed by them at least once.

companies.name: Ferrum Hold Ordnance
companies.blurb: Buys ore and loyalty in equal measure, and sells shells to whoever is closest to using them.

companies.name: Greenhollow Verdite Consortium
companies.blurb: Holds three of the seven verdite claims on Greenhollow. The other four are held by people shooting at them.

companies.name: Ossuary Reclamation
companies.blurb: Cuts up the dead. A rift bloom somewhere else is a good quarter here, and they have stopped apologising for saying so.

companies.name: Choir Reliquary Trust
companies.blurb: Sells Apostle relics to Apostles. Moves on faith, which is a hell of a thing to underwrite.

companies.name: Sib Vael Distilling
companies.blurb: Kelp spirits and reef liquor out of the floating markets. Famous across the Expanse and almost aggressively boring to own.

companies.name: Bexley Agricombine
companies.blurb: Protein, meal brick and water reclamation for the whole frontier. Nobody has ever been excited about this stock and nobody has ever been ruined by it.

companies.name: Cindermoor Refining Charter
companies.blurb: The cartel charter over the magma flats. Choking, wealthy and dangerous, in that order.

companies.name: Coil Transit Authority
companies.blurb: Levies every hull that goes through the gate. Nobody elected them and nobody can stop them.

companies.name: Adler Line
companies.blurb: Nobody will say plainly whose flag this is. Everybody pays it anyway.

companies.name: Smuggler's Gyre Freight
companies.blurb: Freight that does not file a manifest. Prices in the risk and occasionally gets the price wrong.

companies.name: Crater Sea Pilgrim Lines
companies.blurb: Ships the faithful towards the craters. Return traffic is famously light.

companies.name: Emberline Thermics
companies.blurb: Refines hyper-dense thermite for people who intend to put it in something.

companies.name: Tarn Cryogenics
companies.blurb: Ice hauled out, questions not asked. Cheap labour and colder politics.

companies.name: Marrow Water Rights
companies.blurb: Holds paper on the only water anyone has found on Marrow. Paper is not the same as water.

companies.name: Kettle Hollow Meltwater
companies.blurb: A colony carved into a glacier, selling what runs off it. On no registry anywhere, which is a feature until it is not.

companies.name: Anvil Cluster Foundries
companies.blurb: Directorate heavy industry with a civilian letterhead. Hulls, plate and anything that needs to survive being hit.

companies.name: Gallows Reach Bonding
companies.blurb: Underwrites bounties. Pays out when the wrong person comes home.

companies.name: Frostwatch Bonded Escort
companies.blurb: Sells convoy cover in the one volume where the rings blind everybody's scanners. Excellent business model.

companies.name: Pale Reach Mutual
companies.blurb: Writes rift insurance. Has never once had a good year in which a rift opened.

companies.name: Bonefield Salvage Trust
companies.blurb: Pay the yardmaster and pick the bones. Now with shareholders.

companies.name: Rust Belt Reclaimers
companies.blurb: Strips hulks nobody has filed a loss on. Occasionally strips one somebody has.

companies.name: Drowned Span Salvage
companies.blurb: Works the span where the wrecks are thickest and the readings are worst.

companies.name: Thousand Wrecks Consolidated
companies.blurb: Consolidated in the sense that one man now owns all the debts.

companies.name: Nyx Rift Prospecting
companies.blurb: Dives the rift for what is left near the edge. The crews are paid extremely well and extremely often replaced.

companies.name: Wraithlight Assay
companies.blurb: Certifies ore nobody else will touch. Its stamp is worth more than the ore.

companies.name: Ferrun Deep Ore
companies.blurb: Directorate-leaning, orderly, and utterly unwelcoming to anyone with a story.

companies.name: Sallow Cartographics
companies.blurb: One washed-out surveyor, one complete chart of the Reach, and a great many people who would like a copy.

companies.name: Keth Minor Bioprospect
companies.blurb: Holds a claim on an oxygen-rich planetoid with structures on it that nobody built. Pure speculation with a medical letterhead.

companies.name: Vesper Nebula Medical
companies.blurb: Stasis pods, trauma kits and the only reliable field surgeons this side of the Coil.

companies.name: Warmroom Supply
companies.blurb: Sells what the medbay runs out of, at the price the medbay will pay.

companies.name: Satedan Reclamation Fund
companies.blurb: Buys back what was taken off a dead world. There are more survivors than anyone believed, and they are all subscribers.

companies.name: Reliquary Drift Holdings
companies.blurb: Warehouses things it cannot identify and insures them at whatever number somebody will write down.

companies.name: Gilded Veil House
companies.blurb: Tables, rooms and discretion. Owns rather more of its clientele than they would like known.

companies.name: Sundowner Floor Holdings
companies.blurb: A share in the endless casino city itself. You are, in the most literal sense, buying the house.

Heard the {place} tender is going to {name}. Heard it twice, mind.

events.headline: {name} loses the {place} contract to a cheaper hull.
rumours: {ticker} are about to get undercut on {place}. Badly.
A {name} handler was drinking like a man who has read next quarter.

events.headline: Lanes closed around {place}. {name} is on the wrong side of it.
rumours: Directorate hulls forming up sunward of {place}.
Nothing has come out of {place} in two days and nobody will say why.

events.headline: The Frostwatch put inspectors on every {sector} hull out of {place}.
rumours: Watch is stopping {sector} traffic at {place}. Papers, holds, everything.
Somebody tipped the Watch about {ticker}. Somebody usually has.

events.headline: The {place} yards walk out on {name}.
rumours: The {place} crews haven't been paid. Third week.
{ticker} has a labour problem it is calling a scheduling problem.

events.headline: {name} settles with the {place} yards and gets the line running.
rumours: Word is {ticker} is about to settle. Cheap, too.

events.headline: {name} pulls something intact out of {place} and will not say what.
rumours: A {ticker} crew came back off {place} very quiet and very rich.
Something came up out of {place}. Ancient, if you believe the assay.

events.headline: The {name} find is assayed as slag. The market notices.
rumours: That {ticker} relic is a fake. Ask anyone who has held it.

events.headline: Something came through near {place}. {name} lost hulls and crews.
rumours: Readings all wrong out past {place}. Two hulls overdue.
The {ticker} yard is not answering. That is never nothing.

events.headline: A field of fresh wrecks opens near {place}. {name} gets there first.
rumours: There is a wreck field off {place} nobody has filed on yet.
{ticker} has three cutters heading somewhere in a hurry.

events.headline: {sector} runs short across the Expanse. {name} is holding stock.
rumours: Nobody can get {sector} at any price right now.
{ticker} is sitting on a warehouse and smiling about it.

events.headline: {sector} floods the market. {name} is holding the wrong stock.
rumours: Everyone and their brother is carrying {sector} this month.

events.headline: {name} is taken out at a premium.
rumours: Somebody is buying {ticker} quietly. Look at the size of the lots.
There is paper being drawn up over {name}. Big paper.

events.headline: The {name} book turns out to have been fiction for two quarters.
rumours: The {ticker} numbers do not add up. They have not for a while.
A {name} clerk has gone somewhere warm and does not intend to come back.

events.headline: {name} misses a payment it cannot miss.
rumours: {ticker} is being asked for money it does not have.

events.headline: {name} loses the yard, the book and most of the people in it.
rumours: Nobody has heard from the {ticker} yard in two days.
If you own {ticker}, you might want to not own {ticker}.

epitaphs.text: Receivers appointed; the book went for scrap.
Nobody rang a bell. The listing simply stopped answering.
Stripped for the claims and the hull registry, in that order.
It borrowed against a good year that never came.
The yard was cut up by the crews it stopped paying.
The claim went to whoever was still standing on it.
The faithful stopped paying, and faith was the whole balance sheet.
Its hulls are still parked where the lanes closed.
It sold forward against a field that ran dry.
The Watch took the floor, the tables and the ledgers.
One bad month of claims against thirty years of premiums.
A recall it could not survive and would not admit to.
It lost the contract, and the contract was the company.
Two harvests spoiled in the hold and the buyers went elsewhere.

fighters.name: Sump

fighters.name: Needle Ashvane
fighters.gimmick: Fast, thin, and absolutely no margin for a bad night.

fighters.name: Hollowjaw
fighters.gimmick: Came out of a rift zone and has been odd ever since.

fighters.name: The Pale Brother
fighters.gimmick: Apostle stock. Fights like the crater is watching.

fighters.name: Vet Kessik
fighters.gimmick: Twenty years on an ore hauler. Grip like a docking clamp.

fighters.name: Two-Crown
fighters.gimmick: Wears both. Will tell you why at length if you let it.

fighters.name: The Quiet Girl
fighters.gimmick: Nobody has landed a clean one on her in eleven bouts.

fighters.name: Furnace Ott
fighters.gimmick: Cindermoor refinery hand. Hits like the flats and tires like them too.

fighters.name: Cutter Brask
